sentences.text: Harbor Lane Auto Detailing LLC is a California mobile auto-detailing business whose beneficial owner is Marisol Vance; its business checking account ends in 5108.
The account sent a first-time international wire to Bramblecoast Trading FZE, a free-zone trading company with no relationship on file.
The account received 14 posted credits totaling $113,550.55, including 12 cash deposits totaling $112,350.00.
It sent an outbound wire of $98,000.00 to Bramblecoast Trading FZE and an ACH debit of $2,140.00 to its landlord.
The cash deposits occurred from 2026-09-08 through 2026-09-23, and the outbound wire posted on 2026-09-25.
The alert was detected on 2026-09-26, with a filing deadline of 2026-10-26.
The wire beneficiary country was AE.

The activity is inconsistent with expected cash deposits of $2,000–$4,000 a month and card-processor settlements of about $2,500 a month; inflow was 17.5 times expected activity and cash was 37.5 times expected cash activity.
The beneficiary was named in a fictional regulatory notice concerning cash-funded wires against over-invoiced auto-parts shipments.
The customer made 12 cash deposits ranging from $8,800.00 to $9,850.00, including $56,300.00 in cash over a rolling 7-day period without a single deposit at or above $10,000.
A teller recorded that the customer asked how much could be deposited before the bank completed the form and then split the deposit across two days.
The $98,000.00 wire represented 86.3% of all posted credits and was described as an auto-parts invoice payment.

dropped.text: Cash deposits were made at four branches: Oakland Downtown, Emeryville, Berkeley Shattuck, and San Leandro.

rationale.text: The activity matches the structuring typology, with 5 of 5 indicators fired, including repeated cash deposits just under the CTR threshold and cash accumulated above $10,000 in a rolling 7-day period. The activity is also materially inconsistent with the customer's expected profile and includes a large first-time international wire to a beneficiary associated with a trade-based laundering notice.

next_steps: Validate the business purpose and supporting documentation for the $98,000.00 wire without disclosing the review or any SAR consideration.
Review account history and related entities for additional cash deposits, threshold avoidance, or payments involving Bramblecoast Trading FZE.
Assess whether enhanced due diligence or account-risk escalation is warranted under applicable bank procedures.
Preserve the alert, transaction, teller-note, counterparty, and adverse-media evidence for SAR review and filing decision.

sentences.text: Harbor Lane Auto Detailing LLC is a California mobile auto-detailing business whose beneficial owner is Marisol Vance; its business checking account ends in 5108.
The account sent a first-time international wire to Bramblecoast Trading FZE, a free-zone trading company with no relationship on file.
The account received 14 posted credits totaling $113,550.55, including 12 cash deposits totaling $112,350.00.
It sent an outbound wire of $98,000.00 to Bramblecoast Trading FZE and an ACH debit of $2,140.00 to its landlord.
The cash deposits occurred from 2026-09-08 through 2026-09-23, and the outbound wire posted on 2026-09-25.
The alert was detected on 2026-09-26, with a filing deadline of 2026-10-26.
The wire beneficiary country was AE.

The activity is inconsistent with expected cash deposits of $2,000–$4,000 a month and card-processor settlements of about $2,500 a month; inflow was 17.5 times expected activity and cash was 37.5 times expected cash activity.
The beneficiary was named in a fictional regulatory notice concerning cash-funded wires against over-invoiced auto-parts shipments.
The customer made 12 cash deposits ranging from $8,800.00 to $9,850.00, including $56,300.00 in cash over a rolling 7-day period without a single deposit at or above $10,000.
A teller recorded that the customer asked how much could be deposited before the bank completed the form and then split the deposit across two days.
The $98,000.00 wire represented 86.3% of all posted credits and was described as an auto-parts invoice payment.

dropped.text: Cash deposits were made at four branches: Oakland Downtown, Emeryville, Berkeley Shattuck, and San Leandro.

rationale.text: The activity matches the structuring typology, with 5 of 5 indicators fired, including repeated cash deposits just under the CTR threshold and cash accumulated above $10,000 in a rolling 7-day period. The activity is also materially inconsistent with the customer's expected profile and includes a large first-time international wire to a beneficiary associated with a trade-based laundering notice.

next_steps: Validate the business purpose and supporting documentation for the $98,000.00 wire without disclosing the review or any SAR consideration.
Review account history and related entities for additional cash deposits, threshold avoidance, or payments involving Bramblecoast Trading FZE.
Assess whether enhanced due diligence or account-risk escalation is warranted under applicable bank procedures.
Preserve the alert, transaction, teller-note, counterparty, and adverse-media evidence for SAR review and filing decision.
